questions.question: A shopkeeper sells goods at the same price rate for which he has bought them, but gives 20% less quantity to the customer. Find the profit percentage.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A shopkeeper sells goods at the same price rate for which he has bought them, but gives 20% less quantity to the customer.

**Formula used:**

Profit Percentage = dfrac{{Selling Price} - {Cost Price}}{{Cost Price}} times 100 

**Calculation:**

Let Cost Price (CP) for 1 unit be ₹100.

Since the shopkeeper gives 20% less quantity, the quantity given is 80% of the original quantity.

So, the Selling Price (SP) for 0.8 units is ₹100.

SP per unit = dfrac{100}{0.8} = ₹125

Profit = SP per unit - CP per unit

⇒ Profit = ₹125 - ₹100 = ₹25

Profit Percentage = dfrac{25}{100} times 100 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**

questions.question: Two trains are running in opposite directions at the same speed. The length of each train is 180 m. If they cross each other in 12 seconds, what is the speed of each train (in km/h)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **opposite direction**, relative speed = sum of speeds.

Total Distance = Sum of lengths = 180 + 180 = 360 m.

Relative Speed = 360 m ÷ 12 sec = 30 m/s.

Since speeds are **equal**, speed of each train = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 m/s.

Speed in km/h = 15 × (18/5) = 54 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 54 km/h.**

⇒ To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5:

⇒ Speed = 15 × (18 ÷ 5) km/h

⇒ Speed = 3 × 18 km/h

⇒ Speed = 54 km/h

questions.question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 7% per year rate of interest for 3 years.

Net Interest Rate = **Rate** × **Time** = 7% × 3 = 21%

**Principal (P)** = ₹3500

**Rate (R)** = 7% per annum

**Time (T)** = 3 years

⇒ SI = 35 × 21

**∴ The correct answer is ₹735.**

Formula for Simple Interest

Simple Interest (SI) is calculated as SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where **P** is Principal, **R** is Rate, and **T** is Time.

Total Amount

The total sum returned after the loan period is called the **Amount** (A), where A = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI).

Constant Interest Property

In **Simple Interest**, the interest earned remains the same for every year because it is always calculated on the original **Principal**.

Total surface area of hemispherical container = 7392 cm²

The container is 3/4 filled with oil

Radius of small hemispherical bottle (r) = 6.3 cm

Surface area of hemisphere = 3πr²

Volume of hemisphere (V) = (2/3)πr³

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3 × (22/7) × R² = 7392

⇒ R² = 784

⇒ R = √784 = 28 cm

Volume of oil in the container = (3/4) × (2/3)πR³

⇒ Volume of oil = (3/4) × (2/3) × (22/7) × 28³

⇒ Volume of oil = (22/7) × 28 × 28 × 14

Volume of one small bottle = (2/3)πr³

⇒ Volume of one small bottle = (2/3) × (22/7) × 6.3³

Number of bottles required = Total volume of oil / Volume of one small bottle

⇒ Number of bottles = [(22/7) × 28 × 28 × 14] / (2/3) × (22/7) × 6.33

⇒ Number of bottles ≈ 66

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: Find the simple interest on ₹550 for 8 months at 3 paise per rupee per month?

The **rate** of 3 paise per rupee per month is equivalent to **3% per month**.

Total interest for **8 months** = 3% × 8 = **24%**.

Interest = 24% of **₹550** = (24 ÷ 100) × 550 = 0.24 × 550 = 132.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹132.**

**Given:** **Principal (P)** = ₹550, **Rate (R)** = 3 paise per rupee per month, **Time (T)** = 8 months.

⇒ Since ₹1 = 100 paise, Interest in Rupees = 13200 ÷ 100 = ₹132

**∴ The correct answer is ₹132.**

Use the direct ratio formula: **CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%)**

CP / MP = (100 − 25) / (100 + 20) = 75 / 120 = 5 / 8

**Markup Percentage** = [(MP − CP) / CP] × 100

**Profit (P)** = 20%

questions.question: Which of following silver coins was introduced by Sultan Shamsuddin Iltutmish?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tanka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Tanka was a silver coin introduced by Sultan Shamsuddin Iltutmish in the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Iltutmish issued the Tanka in the early 13th century as a part of his currency reforms.
 
• The Tanka weighed about 175 grains (approximately 11 grams) of silver.
 
• This coinage system set the standard for the currency in the Indian subcontinent during the medieval period.
 
• The introduction of the Tanka helped stabilize the economy and facilitated trade within the Sultanate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iltutmish:** Shamsuddin Iltutmish was the third ruler of the Mamluk dynasty in Delhi, known for his administrative and military strategies.
 
• **Currency Reforms:** Iltutmish's introduction of the Tanka and Jittal (copper coins) was part of his effort to streamline and standardize the currency system.
 
• **Economic Impact:** The Tanka contributed significantly to the economic development of the Delhi Sultanate by facilitating trade and commerce.
 
• **Historical Significance:** The Tanka remained in use even after the fall of the Delhi Sultanate, influencing the coinage of subsequent dynasties.
 
• **Standardization:** The weight and purity standards set by the Tanka were adhered to by later rulers, ensuring consistency in the monetary system.

questions.question: Wasifuddin Dagar was associated with which of the following classical music genres?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhrupad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Wasifuddin Dagar is a prominent exponent of **Dhrupad**, a genre of Hindustani classical music.
 
• Dhrupad is one of the oldest forms of North Indian classical music and has its roots in the chanting of Vedic hymns and mantras.
 
• Wasifuddin Dagar belongs to the Dagar family, which has been an integral part of Dhrupad tradition for 20 generations.
 
• He is known for his deep, meditative, and powerful rendition of Dhrupad, continuing the legacy of the Dagarvani style.
 
• Wasifuddin Dagar has performed in various prestigious music festivals in India and abroad, spreading the essence of Dhrupad.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dhrupad:**

 
 
• Dhrupad is characterized by its austere and spiritual nature, focusing on precise intonation and elaborate improvisation.
 
• It includes an extensive Alap (improvisation without rhythm) followed by a composition set to a specific Tala (rhythmic cycle).
 
 
 
• **Ghazal:**
 
 
• A poetic form consisting of rhyming couplets and a refrain, often expressing the pain of loss and the beauty of love.
 
• Ghazals can be set to music, and are popular in both Hindustani classical and semi-classical genres.
 
 
 
• **Tarana:**
 
 
• A style of vocal music in Hindustani classical music where certain words and syllables are used in a fast rendition, often incorporating rhythmic patterns.
 
• It is characterized by the use of mnemonic syllables, such as "ta", "na", "da", and "re".
 
 
 
• **Khyal:**
 
 
• A major vocal style in Hindustani classical music, known for its flexibility and elaborate improvisation.
 
• Khyal compositions are usually based on a specific Raga and are performed in a slow tempo (Vilambit) followed by a fast tempo (Drut).

questions.question: When was the Lahore declaration signed between India and Pakistan?

__
 
• The Lahore Declaration was signed between India and Pakistan on **February 21, 1999**.
 
• This agreement aimed to de-escalate tensions between the two countries and promote peace.
 
• Indian Prime Minister **Atal Bihari Vajpayee** and Pakistani Prime Minister **Nawaz Sharif** were the signatories.
 
• The declaration emphasized the need for both countries to resolve their disputes through **bilateral dialogue** and respect for each other’s sovereignty.

• The Simla Agreement was signed between India and Pakistan on **July 2, 1972**.
 
• It aimed at ensuring peace and stability in the region post the 1971 war.
 
 
 
• **Indo-Pakistani War of 1947-48**:
 
 
• Also known as the First Kashmir War, it was fought between India and Pakistan over the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• The war began in October 1947 and ended in December 1948.
 
 
 
• **Indo-Pakistani War of 1965**:
 
 
• This war was fought between India and Pakistan from April 1965 to September 1965.
 
• The conflict began following Pakistan's Operation Gibraltar, which was designed to infiltrate forces into Jammu and Kashmir to cause insurgency against Indian rule.
 
 
 
• **Kargil War**:

questions.question: According to Global Multidimensional Poverty Index 2022, what was the population of the poor in India in 2020?

• The Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) is published by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** and the **Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)**.
 
• The MPI considers multiple deprivations across health, education, and living standards, offering a comprehensive measure of poverty.
 
• India has shown significant progress in reducing multidimensional poverty over the years, but challenges remain in addressing inequalities.
 
• The report highlights the need for targeted policies to address the various dimensions of poverty and improve overall well-being.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Introduced in 2010, it measures poverty beyond income-based metrics, considering factors like health, education, and living standards.
 
• Each dimension is equally weighted and includes indicators such as nutrition, child mortality, years of schooling, and access to sanitation.
 
 
 
• **Global Trends**:
 
 
• The MPI report provides insights into global poverty trends, highlighting regions and countries that have made significant progress or face major challenges.
 
• Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia are regions with the highest levels of multidimensional poverty.
 
 
 
• **Policy Implications**:

• **Garbha Griha** is the sanctum sanctorum of a Hindu temple where the main deity is enshrined.
 
• It is typically a small, windowless, and dark chamber located at the center of the temple.
 
• The term **Garbha Griha** literally translates to "womb chamber" in Sanskrit, symbolizing the spiritual core of the temple.
 
• Only priests are allowed to enter the Garbha Griha to perform rituals and offer prayers to the deity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stupa**: A Buddhist structure containing relics, typically the remains of Buddhist monks or nuns, used as a place of meditation.
 
• **Shikara**: The spire or tower above the Garbha Griha in North Indian temples, symbolizing the mountain peak and representing the divine abode.
 
• **Mandap**: A pillared hall or pavilion in a Hindu temple used for conducting religious rituals and ceremonies.
 
• The **architecture** and layout of Hindu temples are designed to represent the cosmos, with the Garbha Griha being the focal point.
 
• In South Indian temples, the equivalent of a Shikara is known as the **Vimana**.

questions.question: The 'Rule of Law' is a key feature of the Indian Constitution which is a doctrine ascribed to ________________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Albert Venn Dicey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Albert Venn Dicey, a British jurist, is renowned for his work on the concept of the 'Rule of Law' in his book "Introduction to the Study of the Law of the Constitution" published in 1885.
 
• Dicey outlined three main principles of the 'Rule of Law': the supremacy of law, equality before the law, and the predominance of legal spirit.
 
• The 'Rule of Law' doctrine emphasizes that no one is above the law, and all individuals and institutions are subject to and accountable to the law.
 
• Dicey's concept significantly influenced the legal systems of many democratic countries, including India, where the 'Rule of Law' is a fundamental principle enshrined in the Constitution.
 
• His work laid the foundation for the modern understanding of constitutional law and the protection of individual rights against arbitrary governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Supremacy of Law:** According to Dicey, the law is supreme and no one is above it, including the government itself. This principle is crucial in preventing the abuse of power.
 
• **Equality Before Law:** Dicey emphasized that every person, regardless of status or position, is subject to the same laws and is entitled to the same legal protections.
 
• **Predominance of Legal Spirit:** Dicey argued that the constitution is not the source but the consequence of the rights of individuals as defined and enforced by the courts.
 
• **Indian Constitution and Rule of Law:** The Indian Constitution incorporates the principle of the 'Rule of Law' in its Preamble and the Fundamental Rights, ensuring justice, liberty, and equality to all citizens.
 
• **Judicial Review:** The concept of judicial review in India, which allows the judiciary to review and invalidate laws and actions of the government that violate the Constitution, is derived from Dicey's principles of the 'Rule of Law'.

questions.question: In the periodic table, what is the trend for atomic radius as you move from left to right across a period (horizontal row)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atomic radius decreases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As you move from left to right across a period in the periodic table, atomic radius decreases.
 
• This decrease is due to the increase in nuclear charge (number of protons) which pulls electrons closer to the nucleus.
 
• Despite the addition of more electrons, they are added to the same energy level, resulting in a stronger attraction between the nucleus and the electrons.
 
• The increased effective nuclear charge reduces the size of the electron cloud, thereby decreasing the atomic radius.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Effective Nuclear Charge (Z_eff)**: The net positive charge experienced by an electron in a multi-electron atom, influencing atomic size.
 
• **Shielding Effect**: Electrons in inner shells can shield outer electrons from the full charge of the nucleus, but across a period, the shielding effect does not increase significantly.
 
• **Ionic Radius**: The radius of an atom's ion. Cations (positively charged ions) are smaller than their neutral atoms, while anions (negatively charged ions) are larger.
 
• **Periodic Trends**: Periodic trends are patterns in the periodic table that show the variation in certain properties, such as atomic radius, ionization energy, and electronegativity.
 
• **Atomic Radius Measurement**: Atomic radius is typically measured in picometers (pm) or angstroms (Å), where 1 Å = 100 pm.

questions.question: Who amongst the following said that the government fiscal policy should be used to stabilise the level of output and employment?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• John Maynard Keynes was a British economist whose ideas fundamentally changed the theory and practice of macroeconomics and the economic policies of governments.
 
• Keynes advocated for increased government expenditures and lower taxes to stimulate demand and pull the global economy out of the Depression.
 
• His most important work, "The General Theory of Employment, Interest, and Money" (1936), argued that aggregate demand determines overall economic activity and that inadequate aggregate demand can lead to prolonged periods of high unemployment.
 
• Keynesian economics focuses on using active government policy to manage economic cycles and is considered a demand-side theory that focuses on changes in the economy over the short run.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fiscal Policy:** Government adjusts its spending levels and tax rates to monitor and influence a nation's economy. It is used to achieve macroeconomic objectives such as growth, employment, and inflation control.
 
• **Aggregate Demand:** The total demand for goods and services within a particular market. Keynesian economics suggests that aggregate demand is influenced by public and private economic decisions.
 
• **Great Depression:** A severe worldwide economic depression that took place mostly during the 1930s, originating in the United States. Keynes's theories were developed in response to the economic difficulties of this period.
 
• **Multiplier Effect:** An economic term referring to the phenomenon where an initial injection of spending (usually by the government) leads to increased consumption and hence results in a greater final increase in national income.
 
• **Keynesian Revolution:** Refers to the widespread acceptance during the mid-20th century of Keynes's ideas about how governments should intervene in the economy to manage demand and prevent prolonged recessions.

• **Nutrient Cycling**: The process by which decomposers release nutrients back into the environment, making them available for primary producers like plants.

questions.question: The legislative powers in India are divided into three lists, which are the Union List, the State List and the __________.
questions.solution:

__
 
• The Concurrent List includes subjects of common interest to both the Union and State governments.
 
• It is enumerated in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Both the Parliament and State Legislatures can make laws on the subjects in the Concurrent List.
 
• In case of conflict between the Union and State laws on a Concurrent List subject, the Union law prevails.
 
• Examples of subjects in the Concurrent List include criminal law, marriage and divorce, bankruptcy and insolvency, and education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union List:** Contains subjects of national importance like defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, and railways. Only the Parliament can legislate on these subjects.
 
• **State List:** Contains subjects of local or state importance like police, public health, agriculture, and fisheries. Only the State Legislatures can legislate on these subjects.
 
• **Federal Structure:** India follows a quasi-federal structure, where powers are divided between the central and state governments, with a strong centralizing bias.
 
• **Seventh Schedule:** The division of powers between the Union and State governments is outlined in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution, which contains the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List.
 
• **Residual Powers:** Any subject not mentioned in any of the three lists falls under the residuary powers, which are vested in the Parliament.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

The students were diligently / studying for their exams / for weeks before you arrived.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect tense usage.
 
• The sentence describes an action that continued for a specific duration ("**for weeks**") up to a point in the past ("**before you arrived**").
 
• In such cases, the **Past Perfect Continuous** tense ("**had been + present participle**") must be used instead of the Past Continuous tense.
 
• The correct auxiliary should be "**had been**" instead of "**were**."
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 4** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The students had been diligently studying for their exams for weeks before you arrived."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "No error"** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes, but the tense in part 4 is incorrect.
 
• **2: "for weeks before you arrived"** – This part correctly identifies the duration and the reference point in the past.
 
• **3: "studying for their exams"** – This part is grammatically correct as the present participle form.
 
• **4: "The students were diligently"** – This part contains the auxiliary verb error; "were" should be "had been" to form the Past Perfect Continuous tense.
